newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan police prevent electricity strikers sit-in.
newsitem.headline: Jordan police prevent electricity strikers sit-in.

text.p: Jordanian security forces prevented hundreds of Jordanian electricity workers on Sunday from staging a sit-in in front of the company's head office on the fifth day of a pay strike, union members said.
Eyewitnesses said scores of public security vehicles cordoned off from early dawn the Jordan Electric Power Company compound to bar workers entering the company's head office.
Over 2,000 Electricity Workers Union members have been on strike since Wednesday when the company rejected demands for bonuses that amount to across-the-board rises of at least 20 percent.
The government has said the strike was illegal and warned it might disband the union if it continued, labour ministry officials said.

The governor of Amman, citing security concerns, had earlier authorised the head of the capital's police chief to "take the necessary security measures to prevent any illegal gathering infront of the company headquarters."

"As a result of what happened today and the pressures exerted, the union asked the workers to strike from their homes," said one union source, adding that they were not intimated by the heavy handed measures used by the government.
Efforts by the opposition Islamic Action Front (IAF) to act as mediators between the government and the strikers had failed to produce a breakthrough, union sources said.
The union, part of the 17-member General Federation of Trade Unions, has indirectly threatened a power cut as a last resort if the company and government continued to ignore their demands.
The company says it cannot meet the workers demands which would jeopardise its financial position. The national federation has also criticised the union and called on its members to go back to work.
